legend: Below a grenz zone, there is a diffuse dermal infiltrate of eye-catching Touton giant cells characterized by a wreath of nuclei around a homogeneous eosinophilic centre, with a strongly xanthomatized periphery. Also note the mononuclear macrophages, dominated by xanthomatized cells, less prominent vacuolated cells, and scalloped cells.
Early juvenile xanthogranuloma, with mid-dermal to deep-dermal, ill-defined infiltrate of macrophages.

Early juvenile xanthogranuloma with ill-defined infiltrate of mononuclear, monomorphic vacuolated macrophages. This type of lesion is seen clinically as a solitary lesion of very early xanthogranuloma, as a localized lesion in early benign cephalic histiocytosis, or as a generalized lesion in early generalized eruptive histiocytoma.
A dome-shaped to polypoid lesion of xanthogranuloma with a diffuse, ill-defined dermal infiltrate of mostly massively xanthomatized macrophages.

Below a grenz zone, there is an infiltrate of monomorphic, xanthomatized macrophages, including plentiful Touton giant cells intermingled with a moderate number of lymphocytes. This type of monomorphic lesion is seen clinically as solitary/localized to generalized papular xanthoma, or in the late stages of xanthoma disseminatum. Xanthelasma, which is solitary or localized mostly around the eyelids, follows the same monomorphic xanthomatized reaction pattern, but usually with many fewer (or no) Touton giant cells.
Xanthogranuloma with an ill-defined, diffuse dermal infiltrate of monomorphic, faintly eosinophilic macrophages and some lymphocytes.
A dome-shaped xanthogranuloma with an ill-defined, diffuse dermal infiltrate of macrophages.

Xanthomatized, scalloped, and oncocytic cells are found mostly at the periphery of the lesion, while the central parts are dominated by monomorphic, spindle-shaped macrophages (which are positive for SMA, not shown) arranged in fascicles or a storiform pattern. This type of lesion is seen clinically either as a solitary (adult) xanthogranuloma or as a generalized lesion as part of the presentation of progressive nodular histiocytosis, namely prominent, dermal to subcutaneous, deep-seated nodules to tumours beside superficial more classic papules of xanthogranulomas.

Below a grenz zone, a diffuse dermal infiltrate reveals multinucleate giant cells of (want-to-be) Touton character (mostly missing a xanthomatized rim), beside a polymorphous mixture of mononuclear vacuolated macrophages. Some of the peripheral macrophages are spindle-shaped, and the most prominent are homogeneously eosinophilic, scalloped to oncocytic macrophages.

source: Calzavara P. Division of Dermatology University of Brescia Brescia, Italy

legend: Extensive positive staining for factor XIIIa is typical.
